subtitle: Front-end stack exploration through multiplicity, fit, gaps, spikes, and practitioner routes
centralContract: Compare popular defaults and fit-for-purpose front-end compositions through separate probability objects, dimensional fit, equal low-fidelity spikes, explicit gaps, and reversible decision records.

sourcePage.name: Internal — Simplicity for Humans vs AI — Framework Fit, Swapability & Specification by Example
sourcePage.role: Field Guide source for fit-over-popularity, optionality, swapability, maintainability, and Specification-by-Example posture.

promptCapsule.currentDecision: Choose two front-end stack candidates for equivalent low-fidelity spikes, then preserve evidence and an exit path before a durable stack commitment.

probabilityObjects.label: Generic LLM first-recommendation likelihood
probabilityObjects.statement: P(generic-LLM-first-recommendation | the named prompt condition): the model-verbalized probability that a candidate appears as the first recommendation under that request.
probabilityObjects.normalizationRule: Listed candidates plus other/tail mass sum to one.

probabilityObjects.label: Six-month collaboration fit
probabilityObjects.statement: P(six-month-fit-without-structural-rewrite | declared outcome, team conditions, and current evidence): the contextual planning probability that a candidate supports the selected low-fidelity interaction surfaces for six months while preserving accessibility, semantic readability, maintainability, testability, and a practical replacement path.
probabilityObjects.normalizationRule: Candidate estimates are independent and need not sum to one.

promptCapsule.population: Hybrid human–AI team building accessible, SVG-rich, static collaboration surfaces
promptCapsule.horizon: Six months after the first implementation
conditions: Static hosting is acceptable for the exemplar
The surface includes editable state, JSON and JSON-LD twins, SVG diagrams, and accessible tables
High-risk interaction primitives receive local keyboard and assistive-technology verification
Behavior fixtures remain portable across candidates
The team values optionality over framework popularity
exclusions: A calibrated market-share or model-frequency forecast
A server-heavy application requirement that has not yet appeared
promptCapsule.diversityInstruction: Fan out materially different framework, styling, component, and platform commitments. Include a common LLM default, middle-ground options, a compiler-oriented option, and platform-first options.
promptCapsule.tailInstruction: Reserve explicit mass for viable stacks outside the listed set.
promptCapsule.dimensionInstruction: Score each candidate on the eight named collaboration dimensions. Keep weighted dimensional fit separate from both probability objects.
promptCapsule.gapInstruction: Identify methodological, technical, organizational, evidence, and boundary gaps. Route material technical gaps into practitioner probes, low-fidelity spikes, research, or Core Architectures.
promptCapsule.iterationInstruction: After one run, propose prompt or evidence changes that may raise or lower each probability. Mark these as hypotheses until a successor run or observed spike provides evidence.
promptCapsule.comparisonInstruction: Return candidate correspondence across runs and explain additions, omissions, rank changes, and probability shifts.

dimensions.name: Human maintainability
dimensions.definition: How readily maintainers can understand ownership, debug behavior, and make local changes after the initial implementation.
dimensions.evidenceClass: maintainer walkthrough, code review, change task

dimensions.name: Accessibility integrity
dimensions.definition: How reliably the stack preserves native semantics, keyboard behavior, accessible naming, status feedback, and local assistive-technology verification.
dimensions.evidenceClass: semantic DOM review, keyboard path, AT verification

dimensions.name: Swapability
dimensions.definition: How clearly rendering, styling, components, state, and build layers can be replaced without rewriting unrelated behavior.
dimensions.evidenceClass: replacement spike, dependency and boundary view

dimensions.name: Low-fidelity iteration speed
dimensions.definition: How quickly collaborators can produce, inspect, and revise credible low-fidelity surfaces.

dimensions.name: AI collaboration legibility
dimensions.definition: How well code structure, contracts, examples, and failure states support accurate AI modification and explanation.
dimensions.evidenceClass: cross-model modification task and rationale review

dimensions.name: SVG and data-visual control
dimensions.definition: How directly collaborators can control coordinate systems, grouping, transforms, label placement, interaction, and accessible equivalents.

dimensions.name: Testability and specification fit
dimensions.definition: How easily behavior can be specified independently, tested across layers, and preserved during replacement.

dimensions.name: Operational and dependency calm
dimensions.definition: How well the stack bounds dependency churn, build complexity, resource lifetimes, static deployment, and observability.
dimensions.evidenceClass: dependency review, build test, runtime lifetime audit

candidates.name: React + Tailwind + copied component primitives
candidates.summary: A high-frequency LLM default optimized for immediate scaffolding and familiar examples.

lowFidelitySpikes.name: Semantic form and status feedback
lowFidelitySpikes.decisionQuestion: Can the candidate preserve native form semantics, committed filtering, status feedback, focus recovery, and zero-results messaging with a clear local verification path?
acceptanceCriteria: Native element choice is explicit
Accessible name, description, role, state, and feedback are inspectable
Keyboard path and duplicate-commit boundary are tested
Table or text equivalent is available

react-css-modules-headless.evidence: Shared fixture prepared; local AT verification pending.

svelte-component-css.evidence: Shared fixture prepared; native-first component path pending.

lowFidelitySpikes.name: SVG coordinate and label-placement surface
lowFidelitySpikes.decisionQuestion: Can the candidate render, edit, and export a dense SVG scene while preserving groups, transforms, collision rules, stable IDs, keyboard access, and a table equivalent?
acceptanceCriteria: Geometry lives in a framework-neutral model
Grouped transforms and coordinate conversions are explicit
At least two label-placement methods can be compared
Collision count, runtime, and accessible text map are recorded

react-css-modules-headless.evidence: Direct SVG and grouping path appears viable; dense-scene benchmark remains open.

svelte-component-css.evidence: Compact SVG authoring path appears viable; assistive naming and export checks remain open.

lowFidelitySpikes.name: Responsive comparison and inspector
lowFidelitySpikes.decisionQuestion: Can the candidate preserve semantic order, keyboard reachability, readable tables, and stable inspector identity across narrow and wide viewports?
acceptanceCriteria: No consequential information disappears at narrow widths
Visual order and semantic order remain aligned
Target size and reduced-motion contracts are satisfied
The same artifact state supports visual and table views

react-css-modules-headless.evidence: Responsive chassis and table equivalent pending.

svelte-component-css.evidence: Responsive chassis and table equivalent pending.

lowFidelitySpikes.name: Editable state and JSON / JSON-LD round trip
lowFidelitySpikes.decisionQuestion: Can collaborators edit the surface, export stable state, re-import it, and preserve IDs, value origins, omissions, and source boundaries?
acceptanceCriteria: State JSON validates
JSON-LD parses and preserves stable IDs
Import restores the same consequential state
View configuration remains separate from semantic state

react-css-modules-headless.evidence: Shared state contract available; implementation comparison pending.

svelte-component-css.evidence: Shared state contract available; implementation comparison pending.

lowFidelitySpikes.name: Styling and component-layer replacement
lowFidelitySpikes.decisionQuestion: Can one visual and interaction slice replace its styling or primitive layer while behavior fixtures and domain state remain unchanged?
acceptanceCriteria: Behavior tests remain unchanged
Token and cascade ownership is documented
Replacement work stays inside declared adapters
Migration notes identify changed and preserved elements

react-css-modules-headless.evidence: Replace headless primitive or CSS module in one slice.

svelte-component-css.evidence: Replace component implementation while preserving state and fixtures.

gaps.title: Default-likelihood frequency remains unmeasured
gaps.description: The verbalized default distribution illustrates model priors under two prompts; it is not an empirical benchmark across models or repeated samples.
gaps.consequence: Treating it as measured frequency would overstate precision.
gaps.currentHandling: Preserve as an explicitly uncalibrated distribution and open a benchmark only when the decision needs measured frequency.

gaps.title: Six-month fit combines several forms of evidence
gaps.description: Current fit estimates blend practitioner judgment, design dimensions, and hypothetical spike outcomes without a formal statistical model.
gaps.consequence: Intervals communicate uncertainty but do not establish sampling error.
gaps.currentHandling: Keep dimensional fit visible and reserve formal statistical fit for observed outcomes with a named model.

gaps.title: SVG density and label-placement envelope
gaps.description: The intended scene size, label count, motion pattern, and collision budget remain partially specified.
gaps.consequence: A framework may appear equally suitable in a small sample while diverging under realistic density.
gaps.currentHandling: Run the shared dense SVG fixture and compare at least two placement strategies.

gaps.title: Local assistive-technology verification
gaps.description: Library or framework claims remain source anchors; high-risk primitives still need local keyboard and assistive-technology verification.
gaps.consequence: Accessibility fit can be overstated by source documentation alone.
gaps.currentHandling: Attach local verification to the semantic form and feedback spike.

gaps.title: React version and integration assumptions
gaps.description: React candidates need exact version, rendering, external-store, component-library, and build assumptions before technical claims can settle.
gaps.consequence: A generic React label can hide materially different runtime and coherence behavior.
gaps.currentHandling: Use the React version-coherence probe and record local rendering tests.

gaps.title: Effect and resource-lifetime behavior
gaps.description: Listeners, observers, timers, fetches, and external subscriptions need equal acquire/release review across selected candidates.
gaps.consequence: A concise component model may still conceal duplicated effects or stale resources.
gaps.currentHandling: Run navigation and repeated-render stress cases with an acquire/release ledger.

gaps.title: Maintainer and collaborator context
gaps.description: Current estimates assume a team comfortable with TypeScript, semantic HTML, modern CSS, and local verification; actual experience distribution remains unstated.
gaps.consequence: A stack with strong abstract fit may impose uneven onboarding cost.
gaps.currentHandling: Create a Context Tree for maintainers, designers, accessibility reviewers, and future AI collaborators.

gaps.title: Static-hosting boundary versus server needs
gaps.description: The exemplar assumes a static or mostly client-side collaboration surface; authentication, server rendering, or dynamic API needs could change the candidate set.
gaps.consequence: The selected stack may optimize for a narrower deployment model than future work requires.
gaps.currentHandling: Keep server-capable frameworks in the open tail and revisit when a concrete server requirement appears.

gaps.title: Dependency and six-month aging evidence
gaps.description: The prototype does not yet contain repeated upgrade, security, or dependency-review observations for the candidate stacks.
gaps.currentHandling: Add a dependency review and one controlled upgrade exercise to the spike record.

formalStatisticalFitBoundary.currentState: The surface contains verbalized probability distributions, contextual planning estimates, and weighted dimensional fit. It does not yet contain observed outcome data or a fitted statistical model.
minimumForFormalFit: Observed outcome variable and unit of analysis
Out-of-sample or replication plan where relevant
formalStatisticalFitBoundary.replacementState: When observed spike or pilot data exists, attach a StatisticalFitAssessment while preserving the current verbalized and dimensional records as separate evidence layers.

gapPolicy.determination: Technical gaps are first-class because framework fit depends on runtime, semantics, accessibility, SVG behavior, resource lifetimes, build boundaries, and replacement seams. Methodological gaps remain first-class for sampling, calibration, commensurability, and candidate coverage.

decision.decisionRule: Select two candidates whose combined spike set creates the most information gain across accessibility, SVG control, maintainability, and replacement seams while preserving materially different framework commitments.
decision.rationale: React + CSS Modules + headless primitives represents a high-ecosystem middle ground with explicit seams. Svelte + component-scoped CSS provides a lower-ceremony compiler-oriented contrast. Equal fixtures can reveal whether the additional React ecosystem commitment produces material collaboration value for this surface.
decision.dissentOrMinorityRead: A platform-first Web Components spike may create stronger long-horizon evidence and should enter the next round when the initial two spikes leave swapability or operational-calm questions unresolved.
decision.reviewAfter: After both equal spikes and a Plus / Delta review

publication.note: Candidate values are uncalibrated planning and verbalized-sampling records. They invite replacement with team evidence.

shiftHypotheses.hypothesis: Naming semantic readability, accessibility verification, and swapability reduces the concentration of the utility-class default.
shiftHypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Repeat across models and prompts with the same candidate set.

shiftHypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit layer seams and headless primitive requirements increase both recommendation likelihood and contextual fit.
shiftHypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Compare generated architectures and replacement-spike effort.

shiftHypotheses.hypothesis: Direct SVG authoring and low ceremony become more salient when the collaboration surface is explicitly SVG-rich and static.
shiftHypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Run the dense SVG fixture and compare maintainability and accessibility.

shiftHypotheses.hypothesis: A stronger platform-longevity and interoperability prompt may raise standards-oriented Web Components options from the tail.
shiftHypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Successor run plus one custom-element interoperability spike.
